scenes.headline: How a voice agent answers before you finish talking
scenes.sub: Hugging Face's speech-to-speech: the OpenAI Realtime API as four swappable parts.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Frost! Hugging Face's speech-to-speech is an open voice-agent pipeline. Here's how it plugs into OpenAI clients, and how it starts answering early.

scenes.text: Smart Turn starts transcription and generation before it knows you finished talking, and revision numbers make the wrong guesses invisible.
scenes.say: The idea: start transcribing and answering before it knows you've finished talking, and use revision numbers so the wrong guesses never reach you.

steps.say: An existing OpenAI Realtime client connects by changing one URL. The server speaks the same core events.
Behind it, threads joined by queues. Silero VAD segments the audio, and one of six speech-to-text backends transcribes it.
The language model sits behind an OpenAI-style HTTP boundary, so a local llama server works as well as a hosted one.
One of five text-to-speech backends speaks the reply. Ninety combinations in all.

scenes.title: Smart Turn, speculating on a pause
scenes.say: A voice detector knows that speech stopped, not whether you were finished. Smart Turn judges that from content and prosody.

items.text: Complete turn: start STT and LLM now
items.say: A complete turn starts transcription and generation at once.
An incomplete one waits before spending anything.

items.text: Speech resumes: open a new revision
items.say: If you start talking again, the turn reopens as a newer revision,
and the old revision's work is discarded before you ever hear it.

scenes.quote: This is a tested core subset, not a claim of full OpenAI Realtime API equivalence.
scenes.say: The repo scopes its claim carefully, and CI checks it against OpenAI's own client library. What's missing is any published latency figure.

scenes.text: Implement someone else's protocol exactly enough to be tested against their client, then make everything behind it yours.
scenes.say: So implement someone else's protocol exactly enough to pass against their client, then make everything behind it yours.

recap: Speaks the core OpenAI Realtime events
VAD, STT, LLM, TTS: ninety combinations
Smart Turn speculates; revisions hide wrong guesses
scenes.say: To recap: a borrowed protocol, four swappable parts, and early answers whose mistakes you never hear.
